statement: The owner's rule (2026-09-18): the whole corpus is never run on GitHub-hosted runners when a local alternative exists, releases included. Until now every push whose gate proved only a cone owed a 74-minute corpus run on a hosted runner in the full-corpus canary. The canary now moves local. After a verified push whose gate proved a cone, the publisher starts, detached, a run of exactly the rest of the corpus for the pushed commit - the files the cone did not already prove at that commit, so nothing it just proved runs again - in a fresh exact checkout, where placement spreads it over the lab machines. Green, it records the whole-corpus receipt for that commit; red, the next publish says so before anything else. A newer publish supersedes a running one, as the hosted canary's cancel-in-progress did, because only the newest head matters. The hosted canary runs only when dispatched by hand, and a release proves its exact commit locally and records release-full-v1, so full-gate reuses it rather than waking a remote runner.

constraints.statement: The local corpus runs only what the gate's cone did not prove at the same commit; together they are the whole corpus once.
No workflow runs the corpus on a GitHub-hosted runner unless someone dispatches it by hand.
A red local corpus is shown by the next publish, never silently lost; a lost or superseded run is named as such, not as green.
The publish does not wait for the local corpus, and bookkeeping about it never fails a finished publish.
